Educational mission for learning experience.
Description

SanskarSat-1 is an educational 1U CubeSat mission built to introduce students to real spaceflight. The satellite demonstrates simple optical communication using a bright LED beacon, while teaching core concepts such as telemetry, power management, communications, systems engineering, and responsible space operations through hands-on learning from design to launch and operations.

A 1U CubeSat mission.

  • To enable students and faculty to gain knowledge and experience in the field of Satellite and Space Technology.
  • To empower the Satellite Team with the skills to develop the Satellite through various phases of Design, Analysis, Fabrication and Testing until the Flight Model is made.
  • To maximize the learning experience of the students.
  • To provide a real-time design and development experience for the students on compact space systems.
  • To promote space technology in educational institutions.

The mission complies with ITU provisions 1.56, 1.57, and 25 by operating solely for educational and amateur purposes. It provides hands-on learning for students in satellite design and radio communication. The satellite will operate on amateur frequency (435 MHz ± 64 kHz), allowing global amateur radio operators to receive telemetry, participate in propagation studies, and contribute to technical experimentation. This supports the advancement of amateur satellite service through global collaboration, self-training, and knowledge sharing.
